title: Emrys and the Ledger
premise: When the coffin of Ashford's revered founder, Cornelius Vane, is found empty during a centennial exhumation, retired detective Freya Zhou is pulled back into investigation by an anonymous letter containing a page from a 120-year-old ledger. As Freya decodes the ledger's cipher—hidden in the margins of rare books sold through her own shop—she uncovers that Vane faked his death to escape justice for a buried crime, and that his descendants have been maintaining the lie ever since, silencing anyone who gets close. The final entry points to Vane's living heir, town patriarch Aldous Vane, who has been quietly erasing records and people; Freya must expose him publicly before he destroys the last evidence and her along with it.
about_author: Gideon Crane is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering cold cases and civic scandals before turning to fiction. They live in a converted firehouse full of secondhand books, which they insist are all innocent.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Freya Zhou. During Ashford's centennial ceremony, the founder's coffin is opened for a heritage documentary and found empty except for a brass token stamped with a number. The crowd gasps; the mayor goes pale. Freya watches from her failing bookshop across the square, feeling the old pull of a case she swore she'd left behind. Beat: reluctant awakening.

chapters.title: A Page in the Mail
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. An unsigned letter arrives containing a photocopied ledger page in cipher, with one line translated: 'He never left.' Freya tells herself she'll hand it to the police, but instead cross-references the paper stock and recognizes the watermark of a printer long tied to the Vane family. Her curiosity rekindles something she thought dead. Beat: the hook takes hold.

chapters.title: Margins and Marginalia
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, with a flashback to her forced retirement. She discovers the cipher key hidden in pencil annotations inside rare books her shop bought at auction years ago—the ledger was literally shelved in plain sight. Decoding the first entries reveals payments labeled only as 'the arrangement.' Someone is watching the shop from across the street. Beat: dread beneath discovery.

chapters.title: The Arrangement
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Freya and young archivist Theo Brandt, who asks her to appraise a donated collection. Their decoded entries reveal that in 1904, Cornelius Vane paid hush money after a mill collapse killed eleven workers—a crime blamed on a scapegoated foreman. Freya realizes the 'founder' was a fugitive who staged his own death. Beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: What the Town Owes
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She interviews the last descendants of the foreman, the disgraced Marlowe family, now living on the town's poor edge. Elder Ruth Marlowe recalls her grandmother's warning: 'Never ask about the ledger.' That night, Freya's shop window is shattered and the auction books are gone—stolen. Beat: the cost of asking.

chapters.title: Aldous
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo traces the donation that brought him to Freya back to Aldous Vane, the patriarch who funds the library, the police pension fund, and half the town. Aldous invites Theo to lunch and delivers a velvet threat about 'people who dig up the past.' Theo realizes he's being recruited as a spy—or a sacrifice. Beat: power shows its face.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Following a ledger reference to 'the stone that drinks,' Freya finds a second, unmarked grave on Vane land containing remains and Cornelius's signet ring—proof he died fleeing with the truth, possibly murdered by his own heirs. But the site is disturbed: someone got there first, and left a fresh footprint. Beat: the past fights back.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The police chief, whose salary Aldous quietly underwrites, names Freya a person of interest in the thefts and vandalism. Her license to operate the shop is challenged; allies go silent. Theo arrives at her back door with scanned ledger pages he saved, including the final entry naming 'the keeper' still alive. Beat: isolation before the endgame.

chapters.title: The Keeper
chapters.summary: Climax, Freya's POV. At the centennial gala, Freya publicly decodes the ledger on the hall's projector, revealing the mill cover-up and the empty coffin scheme sustained by four generations of Vanes. Aldous confronts her privately with a pistol, confessing his grandfather murdered Cornelius to protect the name. Theo livestreams from the balcony; the confession goes out to every phone in the square. Beat: truth as a weapon.

chapters.title: Restocking the Shelves
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue tone. Aldous is arrested; state investigators reopen the mill case and clear the Marlowe name. The stolen books are returned, and Freya donates the decoded ledger to a public archive rather than keeping its power. Ruth Marlowe visits the shop, and they share tea in silence. Freya finally closes the last open file—and keeps the shop open. Beat: justice outside the law, peace inside it.
